findings.description: The new `head(f)` helper builds `os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "head", f)` from the `file` column of the labels TSV (via `r["file"]` at line 366 and `p["file"]` at line 384) with no check that the result stays under `<corpus>/<fx>/head/`. `os.path.join` discards the prefix for an absolute `f`, and `..` segments walk out of the tree. The file is opened with `errors="replace"` so any readable file parses. Lines 390-393 then copy `lines[n-1].strip()` verbatim into a new TSV row for every manifest `anchors` entry, and line 418 writes that into the tracked labels file. `has_secret(t)` is the only content filter; `/etc/passwd`, shell history, config lines, internal hostnames, etc. would pass. A branch that ships a labels row with `file=/home/<user>/.bash_history` (or `../../../../etc/hosts`) plus a matching manifest `file` and `anchors` list turns a maintainer's `--sync-labels` run into a local-file exfil into a committed artifact. The manifest/labels `file` equality check at line 381 does not help because both are attacker-controlled in that scenario. The existing `fail(f"{fx}: head/{f} missing")` also acts as a file-existence oracle.
findings.failure_mode: A maintainer runs `--sync-labels pr-NN` on a branch whose labels TSV names a path outside head/. Stripped lines from an arbitrary readable local file are appended as must_match text into labels/pr-NN.tsv, which the maintainer then reviews/commits/pushes. The rebuild-byte-identical check at line 414 passes because build_manifest resolves the same traversal path.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the `file` column once in read_labels (reject `os.path.isabs(f)`, any `..` segment, backslashes, and empty segments) and, in `head()`, resolve `hp = os.path.realpath(...)` and `fail` unless it starts with `os.path.realpath(os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "head")) + os.sep`. Apply the same containment check where build_manifest loads head files so both paths agree.

findings.description: The header documents that a refusal leaves the labels file untouched, and the verify-before-write ordering delivers that for validation failures. The final write, however, is an in-place truncating `open(lpath, "w").write(new)`. A SIGINT, disk-full, or process kill between truncation and completion leaves a partially written or empty labels/pr-NN.tsv, which the next `--build-manifest` or `--check` will then reject, and the only recovery is git. Because `--sync-labels` deliberately does not refreeze SHA256SUMS, the corruption is not caught until a later `--check`.
findings.failure_mode: Interrupted write truncates a tracked labels file; the 'labels left unchanged' guarantee silently fails for crash cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Write to a sibling temp file in LABELS_DIR (e.g. `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=LABELS_DIR, delete=False)`), flush+fsync, then `os.replace(tmp, lpath)` so the update is atomic.

findings.description: The approved_by guard rejects ASCII control characters (`[\x00-\x1f\x7f]`) with the stated goal of a one-line header, but `read_labels` (line 213) parses with `str.splitlines()`, which also breaks on U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. A manifest approved_by containing one of those passes the guard, is interpolated into the header at line 398, and re-parses as two lines, the second of which can be shaped like a TSV data row or comment. The rebuild comparison at line 414 does refuse the write (the rebuilt approved_by is truncated and can never equal the manifest value), so there is no exploitable outcome today, but the primary check is not doing what it claims and the resulting error blames an approved_by mismatch rather than the injected line break.
findings.failure_mode: Defense-in-depth only: an attacker-controlled manifest produces a confusing refusal instead of a clear rejection; if the byte-identical rebuild check were ever relaxed, header-line injection into the labels TSV would become possible.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the control-char regex with `len(approved_by.splitlines()) != 1 or not approved_by.isprintable()` (or additionally reject `\x85  `), matching the splitting behaviour read_labels actually uses.
